solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: German delicacy beginning to lessen in hot bar

indicators.note: in signals that one letter goes inside the word for stolen goods

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen, as with hot goods

indicators.note: beginning to points to only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a cake of soap is a bar of it

explanation.surface: A German treat whose start shrinks while it sits in a warm bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like temperature but is slang for stolen goods; 'beginning to' takes the first letter of lessen, and a bar of soap is also a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a fruit loaf from Germany eaten at Christmas, a classic festive delicacy.

clue.text: Dodgy religious group grabbing American power

indicators.note: grabbing means the group's word holds the others inside

parts.note: a sect is a religious faction
US means American
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A shady cult seizes control of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dodgy is questionable or not to be trusted, i.e. of doubtful honesty.

clue.text: Ordinary space is egg‑shaped

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A plain gap turns out to be oval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from the Latin for egg and describes an oval, egg-like form.

clue.text: Bookkeeper from Iran ruined by Blair being reckless

indicators.note: being reckless suggests the letters of Blair behave wildly into a new order
ruined means the letters of Iran are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Iran is wrecked by a careless Tony Blair, the former British Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being reckless' rearranges BLAIR to LIBRA and 'ruined' rearranges IRAN to RIAN; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after books, so is literally a keeper of books, not an accountant.

clue.text: River and province on the borders of Lille

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

indicators.note: on the borders of picks the outside letters of the French city

explanation.surface: A river and a region lie at the edges of the French city of Lille.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is called 'the Province' in Britain; 'on the borders of' gives L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of Egypt and north-east Africa.

clue.text: So Arsenal, playing without energy, will be runners-up

indicators.note: playing signals rearranging, and without says one letter is removed first

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the London football club, are playing badly and will finish second.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from SO ARSENAL and 'playing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Also-rans are those who finish behind the winners, the unplaced competitors.

clue.text: Student drops out of studies and makes money

indicators.note: drops out of says one letter leaves the word for studies

parts.note: learns means studies
L is a learner, from the learner driver plate

explanation.surface: A student quits college and starts earning instead.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner (as on British learner-driver plates) 'drops out of' LEARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive pay for work, so it means making money.

clue.text: Medical cover for group with a case of gangrene

parts.note: a band is a group

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of the word, like a casing

explanation.surface: A dressing is needed for a crowd with an instance of gangrene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives G and E, the outside of gangrene.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material wrapped over a wound, a covering used in medicine.

clue.text: Combo regularly playing violin in limbo

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the band word
playing means the letters of violin are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A small band keeps strumming a violin in a state of uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O and B from combo; 'playing' turns VIOLIN into LIVION.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of neglect or being forgotten, which matches oblivion.

clue.text: Drinks made from mushrooms?

definitions.meaning: a snowball is a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade, popular at Christmas
as a verb, to mushroom is to grow very rapidly

explanation.walkthrough: 'mushrooms' looks like a noun, as if the drinks were brewed from fungi; it is the verb meaning grows fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a Christmas cocktail plural, and the verb for growing fast like a rolling ball of snow.

clue.text: Bird runs home clutching old book

indicators.note: clutching means the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
in means at home
OB stands for old book

explanation.surface: A bird dashes back to its nest carrying an antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common garden songbird, so a bird in general names it by example.

clue.text: Make lovable teens dye hair regularly

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Adolescents colour their hair to look more charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on from teens dye hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them liked or loved, a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: One about to chase money for vegetables

indicators.note: to chase means the following pieces run along behind the word for money

parts.note: brass is northern English slang for money
I is the Roman numeral for one
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to pursue cash for some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' here is northern British slang for cash; 'to chase' puts one and about behind it, since chasing means following.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the plant genus of cabbages, sprouts and broccoli, so it covers many vegetables.

clue.text: Cold shoulder sent back before relations eat

indicators.note: sent back means the word for snubbing is read backwards

parts.note: to give someone the cold shoulder is to cut them
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives are snubbed and turned away just before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses CUT to TUC, followed by KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck in is an informal idiom for starting to eat heartily.

clue.text: Have a riotous time with left luggage here

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and party noisily

explanation.surface: Party wildly and leave your bags here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left luggage' reads as a British station office where bags are stored; left is only L.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, bags circulate on a rotating belt, the place where luggage is collected.

clue.text: Resting during perfomance, wives undressed

parts.note: in means during
an act is a performance

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: Wives with no clothes on are idle in the middle of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips W and S from wives, leaving IVE. The clue as printed misspells performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is resting is out of work, that is, not currently active.

clue.text: Castro's first up-to-date planned takeover

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Castro's
planned suggests the letters of up-to-date are arranged to a scheme

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro's modern, carefully plotted seizure of power.
explanation.walkthrough: C from Castro's, then 'planned' rearranges UPTODATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is a sudden seizure of government, i.e. an illegal takeover of a state.

clue.text: Order for military logs to be burnt here

definitions.meaning: a grate in a hearth where logs burn

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a command telling soldiers to shoot and a hearth fire burning in the open.

clue.text: Norm cuts roots

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
snips means cuts

explanation.surface: A standard rule cuts back the roots of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables, so roots names them as an example of the class.

clue.text: A bit of sleep as southerners complete military training

indicators.note: a bit of means a piece taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Southern soldiers grab a quick nap after finishing their drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' points to letters inside sleep as southerners; 'sleep' tempts towards a definition of fainting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets pass out at a parade marking the end of training, a British military idiom.

clue.text: Put out by short question in front of magistrates, losing head

parts.note: QU is a short form of question

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the bench is the body of magistrates in court

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissed after a brief query before the court.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the magistrates sitting in court are collectively the bench; 'losing head' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To quench a fire is to extinguish it, so put out is a synonym.

clue.text: Distribute shares, including new tackle

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters take the extra letter inside
distribute suggests spreading the letters of shares into a new order

explanation.surface: Hand out stock, along with some fresh fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribute' rearranges SHARES to HARESS, and 'including' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Harness is the straps and gear for a horse, which is one sense of tackle.

clue.text: Beating an investment in Turkey?

definitions.meaning: the question mark hints at a filling put inside a roast bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the country, so investment suggests finance; it is the Christmas bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffing is a thrashing in sport, and also the filling cooked inside a roast bird.

clue.text: A spent force in Germany's neighbour?

definitions.text: A spent force in Germany's neighbour?

parts.words: A spent force in Germany's neighbour?
parts.note: money once used across the Rhine from Germany, now replaced by the euro, so spent in two senses

explanation.walkthrough: 'spent force' suggests someone finished; here it is money that was spent and is now out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: The country west of Germany used this currency until the euro arrived, so it is money no longer in circulation.

clue.text: Journalist travelled back across city centre

indicators.note: across means the reversed word spans the other piece
back means the word for travelled is read backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled, on a horse or vehicle

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of city

explanation.surface: A reporter retraced their route right through the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city centre' means the two middle letters of city, not a downtown area; 'back' reverses the riding verb and 'across' wraps it round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor works on a newspaper, so is a kind of journalist.

clue.text: School transport

definitions.meaning: to school someone is to teach or coach them

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to instruct; as a noun it is a railway vehicle.

clue.text: Land in water

parts.note: a piece of ground surrounded by sea

explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a small island, a piece of ground surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Love game played in end of series

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of game are put into play in a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis match won to love finishes off a run of games.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring; 'played' rearranges game. The definition fits because the Greek alphabet ends with this letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the final item in a sequence.

clue.text: Unable to get enough at sea in it, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone out on the ocean can never be satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of AT SEA IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate is an older form of insatiable, describing an appetite that cannot be satisfied.

clue.text: Miner's daughter gets son fruit

parts.note: in the folk song Oh My Darling, Clementine, she is the daughter of a miner, a forty-niner

explanation.surface: A mining family's girl hands her boy some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clementines are small citrus fruits, like mandarins, common at Christmas.
